newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine employment up 1.6 pct in 1996 - official.
newsitem.headline: Argentine employment up 1.6 pct in 1996 - official.

text.p: Argentine employment grew by 0.4 percent in December with respect to November, taking the total rise for 1996 to 1.6 percent, according to a report by the Labor Ministry released Monday.

"The December increase was more evenly spread across different sectors than in the previous months, as only the construction sector performed badly," said the report, which was based on a survey of 200 firms throughout the country.

While construction employment fell by 0.8 percent, employment in commerce, restaurants and hotels rose by 0.7 percent. The number of jobs in transport, warehouses and communications rose by 0.6 percent, and in municipal, social work and services by 0.5 percent.
While the number of jobs in services rose throughout 1996, other employment fell.
Employment in the financial sector rose by 9.9 percent and in restaurants and hotels by 6.5 percent. But jobs in construction fell by 11.5 percent.
The report said that the average number of hours worked by employees rose in 1996, helping to explain why the unemployment rate is still stuck at 17.3 percent.
There was also a tendency for employers to switch from hiring fixed-term to more flexible contracts.
The percentage of workers hired on a trial basis or on flexibile contracts doubled during the year to 13.3 percent, the report said.
